predecessors.name: Great Seljuk Empire
predecessors.text: Mosul and al-Jazira, the atabegate the Seljuks gave Zengi in 1127

predecessors.name: Artuqids
predecessors.text: Aleppo, taken from the Artuqids in 1128

successors.name: Ayyubid Sultanate
successors.text: Damascus (November 1174) and Aleppo (12 June 1183); Egypt had been Saladin's since 1169 in Nur ad-Din's name

successors.name: Mongol Empire
successors.text: Mosul, taken by Hülegü's army after a nine-month siege and destroyed in 1262

ledger.x: 1127: the Seljuks make Zengi atabeg of Mosul, in charge of al-Jazira and northern Syria.
1128: Zengi takes Aleppo from the Artuqids and unites it with Mosul.
1130: Zengi takes Hama.
1137: Zengi wins at Ba'rin and takes Montferrand from the County of Tripoli.
1138: Zengi agrees terms with Damascus (May), marries Zumurrud Khatun and receives Homs as her dowry.

1139: Zengi takes Baalbek after promising safe passage and not honouring it ("Zengi did not keep his word to protect his captives at Baalbek in 1139"); "The territory went to Najm al-Din Ayyub" (Saladin's father) as governor.
1144: Zengi takes Edessa on 24 December after a four-month siege.
1149: after the victory at Inab (29 June) Nur ad-Din takes the Antiochene land east of the Orontes.
1150: Nur ad-Din conquers the remnants of the County of Edessa west of the Euphrates.
1154: Nur ad-Din takes Damascus from the Burids with the help of its people, unifying Syria "from Edessa in the north to the Hauran in the south".
1154: Nur ad-Din makes Damascus his capital.
1158: Baldwin III retakes Harim for Antioch.
1164: Nur ad-Din "later besieged and captured Banias" after Harim; the page gives no separate date.
1164: Nur ad-Din wins at Harim (12 August) and takes the fortress.
1169: Shirkuh takes Egypt in Nur ad-Din's name and Saladin succeeds him as vizier of the Fatimid caliph.
1171: the Fatimid caliphate is abolished on 17 September; the Nur ad-Din page has "the Fatimid Caliphate was abolished in 1171".
1171: Saladin's Egypt continues as Nur ad-Din's nominal vassal after the end of the Fatimids.
1174: Nur ad-Din dies on 15 May and Saladin's fealty ends with him.
1174: Saladin takes Damascus.
1174: with Damascus lost (27 November) the Zengid seat is Mosul again; infobox "Mosul (until 1234)" and "Damascus (1154-1174)".
1175: Saladin takes Homs and Hama.
1175: Baalbek passes to Saladin.
1177: Aleppo's as-Salih buys off Philip of Flanders and Bohemond III, who besieged Harenc in December: "As-Salih paid 50,000 dinars and renounced half of the nearby villages in favor of Bohemond."
1182: Saladin conquers the Jazira.
1182: Sinjar "was taken by the Ayyubids in 1182.
1183: Imad al-Din Zengi II hands Aleppo to Saladin on 12 June.
1183: in the exchange for Aleppo (handed over 12 June) Saladin restores Sinjar, Nusaybin and Raqqa.
1234: Badr al-Din Lu'lu' ends the Zengid line at Mosul and rules in his own name; the emirate of Mosul continues.
1250: the Ayyubid emir of Aleppo takes the Jazira of the last Zengid line, the Sinjar branch.
1262: Hülegü takes Mosul in July after a nine-month siege and destroys it.
1262: the emirate of Mosul, last survivor of the Zengid state, ends with the Mongol capture.

wars.name: Zengi's conquests in Syria
wars.outcome: Aleppo from the Artuqids (1128), Hama (1130), Homs as a dowry (May 1138), Baalbek (July 1139); sieges of Damascus in 1135 and 1139-1140 failed.

wars.name: Battle of Ba'rin
wars.outcome: Zengi defeated Fulk of Jerusalem; Montferrand was permanently lost.

wars.name: Siege of Edessa (1144)
wars.outcome: Zengi took Edessa on 24 December 1144 after a four-month siege; the county's remnant west of the Euphrates fell to Nur ad-Din in 1150.

wars.name: Nur ad-Din's wars with the Crusader states
wars.outcome: Inab (29 June 1149) defeated Raymond of Poitiers and gave Nur ad-Din the Antiochene land east of the Orontes, Harim included; Banias besieged in 1157; Baldwin III retook Harim in 1158; Raynald of Chatillon captured in 1160; Harim (12 August 1164) and Banias…

wars.name: Zengid conquest of Damascus
wars.outcome: Nur ad-Din overthrew the Burid ruler "in 1154, with help from the city's population".

wars.name: Shirkuh's expeditions to Egypt
wars.outcome: Shirkuh invaded in 1164, 1166 and again at the beginning of 1169; Amalric invaded in 1167 and 1168; Nur ad-Din's commander gained full control in 1169 and Saladin succeeded Shirkuh.

wars.name: Saladin's conquest of Zengid Syria
wars.outcome: Damascus (27 November 1174), Homs (March 1175), the Horns of Hama (13 April 1175) and Hama by mid-1175, Aleppo's recognition of Saladin (spring 1176), Aleppo handed over on 12 June 1183 in exchange for Sinjar, Nusaybin and Raqqa.

wars.name: Saladin's campaigns against Mosul and the Jazira
wars.outcome: In 1182 Edessa, Saruj, Raqqa, Qirqesiya and Nusaybin fell to Saladin and Kukbary of Harran defected; he besieged Mosul from 10 November 1182 (it held) and took Sinjar on 30 December 1182 after 15 days; in 1183 Sinjar, Nusaybin and Raqqa were restored to Zengi…

wars.name: Mongol conquest of Mosul
wars.outcome: Lu'lu' supplied Baiju's troops in 1258 and submitted to Hülegü; his son revolted after Ain Jalut (1260); Hülegü besieged Mosul nine months and destroyed it in 1262.

certainty.note: Atabegates, tributary cities and moving sieges; the pages give no treaty line except the Orontes frontier with Antioch after 1164.
